description: NIFS is Gemini's near-infrared integral-field spectrograph. These six curves are the ZJ, JH and HK blocking filters, each scanned at room temperature and at 77 K.
facility_description: NIFS is used on the Gemini North 8.1 m telescope on Maunakea, operated by Gemini Observatory. It is an infrared integral-field spectrograph with a HAWAII-2RG detector.
notes: The components page says the gratings are used with one dual blocking filter: Z-J, J-H or H-K. The ZJ.dat header lists cut-on and cut-off at both temperatures and labels the columns 298 K and 77 K. The page also lists KG3 and KG5 neutral-density filters in the focal-plane unit; those are not these six bands. McGregor et al. 2003, Proc. SPIE 4841, is the instrument paper. The page describes the detector as a Rockwell HAWAII-2RG HgCdTe array and contrasts it with CCDs. No magnitude system is stated.

ZJ_298K.Description: NIFS ZJ blocking filter at 298 K
ZJ_298K.Comments: Gemini filter table: ZJ, Gemini ID G0601, central wavelength 1.11 μm, coverage 0.77-1.44 μm. ZJ.dat's header names it the Z-J filter and gives two transmission columns, labelled 298 K and 77 K; this band is the 298 K column. The components page says the gratings are used with one dual blocking filter: Z-J, J-H or H-K.
